newsitem.title: USA: Mattel plans to "pare" non-core brands.
newsitem.headline: Mattel plans to "pare" non-core brands.

text.p: Mattel Inc chief executive officer Jill Barad said Mattel will "pare back" its non-core brands which have had sagging sales and turn more attention on its stronger core brands, like Barbie and Hot Wheels.
She declined to say if charges or writedowns would result.

"We're now in the process of evaluating plans," Mattel chief executive officer Jill Barad said on a conference call. "We'll see erosion in average growth (in early 1997) because we'll be managing out of some of these businesses, but we expect this year to be strong," she said.
Several analysts expect Mattel will take charges. "I suspect there will be charges associated with this refocusing," said Jill Krutick, analyst with Smith Barney.
Barad said about 87 percent of Mattel's business is in core brands, which also include Fisher-Price and Disney brand toys. Worldwide sales of these brands rose 10 percent in 1996.
"The other part that makes up 100 percent of our brands are actually down year over year," said Barad."
"We put a tremendous amount of people, advertising overhead in terms of marketing, design, devlopment, selling, on those other businesses," Barad said.

"We're talking about paring some of that in these other businesses so that we can take some of those savings and put them towards our core brands and take some of those savings and put towards the bottom line," she said.
She would not say which non-core brands might be cut.
A Mattel spokesman said some non-core brands include games like Scrabble and UNO and its Wham-O brands, which include products like hoola hoops and Frisbee.
Mattel took a fourth quarter $8 million charge for its Cabbage Patch Kids Snacktime dolls that were pulled from shelves after some kids' hair got caught in the mouths.
Barad said there had been no backlash from its retail customers regarding those Cabbage Patch dolls.
"The overriding perception is that we did the right thing and we did it voluntarily," she said, noting that sales of the Cabbage Patch doll line overall remain strong.
"We see a worldwide focus with more exciting introductions," she said.

Mattel also took a $15.1 million accounting charge in the fourth quarter. After these items, fourth quarter net was $113 milion versus $112 million and net sales were $1.19 billion verus $1.16 billion a year earlier.
An attorney for Mattel said: "We continue to have every belief that the merger will close in the first half of this year."
Barad said: "Our focus is to focus on core brands and maximize earnings. This new business rationale may affect our first quarter."
